    ho99o9, N8 NoFace, slay squad

    6:00 PM · Garden Amphitheatre, Garden Grove · $33.97

    Ho99o9 (pronounced Horror) is an American punk rap duo founded in 2012 in Newark, New Jersey, by theOGM and Yeti Bones (also known as Eaddy). They have released multiple EPs, accompanied by grindhouse-style music videos, and three full-length albums, United States of Horror (2017), SKIN (2022) and Tomorrow We Escape (2025). N8NOFACE is a Tucson, Arizona--raised musician and rapper now based in Long Beach, California, known for blending gritty punk with lo‑fi hip‑hop into a dark, personal, and often surreal sound Slay Squad formed in 2013, initially starting as a hip-hop group before evolving into a rap metal collective. Their music blends rap, metal, and hip-hop, a style they describe as "ghetto metal," reflecting both aggressive energy and underground influences.

More details emailed to ticket purchasers prior to event date. ABOUT THE THEME: This past year has reminded us how deeply our lives are woven together. Across the world, families have endured separation, communities have mourned, and many have searched for peace, comfort, and healing. In times of sorrow, we are reminded that suffering knows no borders---and neither should compassion. Yet even in difficult times, there are moments that draw us closer. Through music, art, tradition, celebration, and remembrance, people gather across cultures and continents to share joy, offer comfort, and dream together. In those moments, the distance between us seems to disappear, revealing the bonds that have always connected us. The same sun rises over each of us. The same moon watches over those we love. The same stars that guided our ancestors continue to shine above us today. Wherever we may stand upon this earth, we are all bajo un mismo cielo --- under one sky. Día de los Muertos reminds us that love knows no borders. Memory belongs to us all. Grief belongs to us all. Hope belongs to us all. When we gather to honor our ancestors, we are reminded that every life leaves behind a story---and every story is worthy of being remembered.

    Saturday 24th 5pm CANELONES Argentina. 91m. Dir. Christian Basilis y Ana Laura Gussoni. During their teenage years in Mercedes, Hernán and his friend Chiri stave off boredom by making prank calls to neighbors. One of these calls crosses the line, deceiving a mother into believing her absent son is coming home for dinner; she prepares cannelloni that go uneaten, and some time later, she takes her own life. Saturday 24th 8pm YO, NARCISO Argentina. 95m. Dir. Adrian Suar. The story follows Rocío Flores (Natalia Oreiro), a sociology professor who decides to investigate modern narcissism. For her study, she chooses Máximo Rey (Adrián Suar) a charismatic and egocentric plastic surgeon as her subject. Rocío goes undercover using a false identity, posing as a patient. However, the experiment becomes complicated when Máximo falls in love with her and the situation spirals out of control.

    Argentine Film Festival Supported by The Miracle Theater Foundation

    4:00 PM · The Miracle Theater, Inglewood

    Sunday 25th 4pm PEPITA, LA PISTOLERA Argentina. 103m. Dir. Lucia Puenzo. Set in Mar del Plata during the winter of 1985. It follows the life of Margarita Di Tullio, a sex worker and expectant mother who confronts exploitation rings, local mafias, and corrupt police. The plot takes on historical significance when she defends herself and kills three criminals who break into her home a real-life event that turns her into one of the most famous and controversial figures in the Argentine underworld. Sunday 25th 7pm LO DEJAMOS ACA Argentina. 98m. Dir. Hernan Goldfrid. A pragmatic psychoanalyst, disillusioned with traditional methods, begins to cross ethical boundaries with his patients until he takes on a new patient: a writer suffering from writer's block and alcohol problems.
